_comment: Work by other people that this pack stands next to, and what is being attributed to each.
The pack is published into a field that already has serious work in it. Shipping with no
acknowledgement would read as unaware, and it would be the one claim in the pack a reader
could not check -- which is the opposite of everything else here. So attribution is a
registered artifact rather than a paragraph of goodwill.
EVERY ENTRY CARRIES THE VERSION IT WAS READ AT AND THE DATE IT WAS READ, for exactly the
reason verified-against.json demands the same of claims about the harness. A claim about
somebody else's repository is a claim about a moving artifact: it releases, it renames its
skills, it corrects its own guidance. An undated description of another project is not a
citation, it is a memory -- and it goes false the same silent way an undated harness claim
does, with the sentence carrying it never changing.
'reason' is required, and the wording is borrowed from external-citations.json on purpose: an
entry nobody justified is a silencer, not a decision. Here the thing it protects against is
narrower and worse -- attribution decorates. It gets written once for credit, the field moves,
and it sits on the page flattering nobody while looking like diligence. A reason is what lets
the next reader decide whether an entry is still doing work or is just polite.
SO THIS IS CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, like the citation and sourcing registries before it.
Forward: a work named in PRIOR-ART.md with no entry here fails, so the document cannot grow a
comparison that nobody dated. Reverse: an entry whose 'cited_in' document no longer mentions
the work fails as STALE, so an attribution cannot outlive the paragraph it was written for and
keep collecting credit for a comparison that has been deleted. The reverse half is the quieter
of the two and the reason this file is a registry at all -- one direction only would let a dead
entry persist forever, which is indistinguishable from an entry still doing its job.
'relationship' is one of complementary / convergent / contrast, and it is the field to be
honest in. complementary = a different layer that composes with this one. convergent = reached
the same conclusion separately, which is the strongest evidence either work has and is only
worth counting BECAUSE the authorship was independent (see GIT-AND-REVIEW.md section 4 --
agreement is informative to the extent the errors are uncorrelated). contrast = a real
difference, which must be stated as a difference and not as a verdict on somebody's work.
ONE ENTRY PER WORK, deliberately, even where more than one relationship applies. The
superpowers entry is complementary at the top line and carries its convergence AND its
contrast inside 'claim', because splitting one work across three entries would make the
reverse check ambiguous about which of them a citation had satisfied -- and an ambiguous
reverse check is a reverse check that passes.
'work' IS A VERBATIM SUBSTRING OF THE CITING DOCUMENT, and that is a constraint on this field
rather than a coincidence. The reverse check finds an entry's citation by looking for the work
in the document, so a 'work' dressed up with a publisher suffix the prose never writes ('Best
practices for Claude Code (Anthropic)') would report the entry as uncited while the citation
sat two lines away -- red for the wrong reason, which costs as much as green for the wrong one.
The publisher belongs in 'claim' and in the prose, both of which say Anthropic. Same trap as
the marker matching in verified-against.json: a name quoted almost-exactly is a different
string, and only the exact one is checkable.

entries.claim: The prior work on disciplined agentic coding that this pack sits closest to, and the primary comparison. It is the WORKFLOW layer -- brainstorming, git worktrees, written plans, subagent-driven execution with two-stage review, RED-GREEN-REFACTOR, code review, branch completion -- shipped as auto-triggering skills through a plugin marketplace and enforced by skill instructions in the model's context. This pack is the verification and harness layer beneath it, so they compose rather than compete. Three specific attributions: (1) the layer distinction above; (2) CONVERGENCE, twice over -- its v6.3.0 fix stopping worktree removal from destroying untracked files, and asking instead, is independently the conclusion of REVERSIBILITY.md sections 5-6 and the worktree toolkit's naming of untracked files plus its non-destructive in-use probe, while its stated principle 'Evidence over claims - Verify before declaring success' is this pack's own thesis in other words; (3) CONTRAST, on claim hygiene only -- its writing-skills skill asserts internals of the tools it runs on (frontmatter 'Max 1024 characters total', a description kept 'under 500 characters if possible', per-category word budgets, and that some skills load into every conversation) with no version or date on any of them.
entries.reason: Protects against the failure a reviewer who knows this field spots in the first minute: a pack about verification discipline, published with no acknowledgement of the best-known methodology on the same subject, reads as unaware -- and being unaware of prior art is the one deficiency this pack's own evidence rules cannot excuse. It also holds the pack to its own standard in the direction that costs something. The convergence is the strongest evidence either project has for these rules and had to be stated generously rather than absorbed; the contrast is about DATING and had to be kept off correctness, because their numbers may be right and the point survives either way. Everything above was read at v6.3.0 (published 2026-08-12; the default branch was level with that tag, zero commits ahead) on 2026-08-19. Re-read the release notes and skills/writing-skills before touching this entry -- a project shipping releases this often will move, and bumping date_checked without re-reading is the drift the pack exists to prevent.

entries.version_checked: living documentation page, no version or date shown on the page itself
entries.claim: Anthropic's own published guidance arrives at this pack's thesis from a third direction: 'Give Claude a way to verify its work', 'the trust-then-verify gap' named as a common failure pattern, and the instruction to have Claude show evidence rather than assert success. Cited in PRIOR-ART.md as the third leg of the convergence argument, and as the reason the field is not a two-project field.
entries.reason: Two jobs. It stops the section reading as though one other project exists, which would be its own kind of unawareness. And it is the vendor's own material converging on the rule, which is the least correlated agreement available here -- different author, different purpose, no shared failures. Recorded with its state rather than a version because it HAS no version: a living docs page carrying no date is the same hazard verified-against.json pins against, met in the source those pins cite, and saying so is more useful than pretending a URL is a release.

entries.version_checked: engineering post dated by its publisher 2025-09-11
entries.claim: Argues for fewer and higher-impact tools rather than a wrapper per API endpoint, clear namespacing so an agent cannot confuse them, returning only high-signal context, token efficiency through pagination and truncation, and evaluating a tool surface rather than assuming it correct. That is CODING-WITH-CLAUDE-CODE.md section 6 -- the tool surface is an input, and it is the one that fails quietly -- reached separately and stated as design guidance rather than as an incident report.
entries.reason: The front door's tool-surface section is the one most likely to be read as an idiosyncratic lesson from one stack's MCP servers. It is not: the same conclusions are published guidance, from an author with a completely different vantage point. Registered so that the convergence is on the record with a read date, and so a later reader can check whether the post still says what this entry claims it says rather than trusting a paraphrase. The publisher's own date is kept separate from date_checked on purpose -- one is when it was written, the other is when somebody here last looked, and collapsing them would hide which of the two had gone stale.
